establishment of an inland navigation company, I have to state
that the inaugural meeting of the new Sino-Japanese concern
known as the "Shanghai Inland River Navigation Company" (capital
Yen 2,000,000) was held at the Japanese Club, Boone Road,
at 2.30 p.m. July 28, 1938, and was attended by promoters
and representatives of the Japanese Army, Navy, Consulate-
General and the Reformed Government of the Chinese Republic
During the meeting Mr. K. Sugimoto, manager of the "Shanghai
Transportation Company", was elected managing director, while
Mr. K. Nakayama, managing director of the "Nisshin Kisen
Kaisha", Mr. T. Yamamoto, vice-president of the Shimonoseki
Chamber of Commerce and Industry, and a Chinese were elected
directors. The name of the Chinese director has not been
disclosed in view of the recurrence of unfortunate incidents
involving pro-Japanese Chinese. It was also decided that
the position of the presidency would be left vacant for the
time being.

The object of the new concern is to undertake the
transportation of passengers and cargo, the renting and
chartering of vessels, the operation of wharves and godowns
in the interior. The office of this concern will be
established in the Darring Apartments on Tsungping Road and
the business will be commenced on August 1. Regular
services between Shanghai and inland towns as mentioned in
the attached translation will be undertaken. The company
will hold a monopoly over inland river navigation in the
district in the vicinity of Shanghai and will take over the
interests and property of the Chinese Shipping Bureau. No. 6

December 12, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

JAPANESE TO FORM LARGE SHIPPING COMPANY FOR YANGTZE
TRADE

According to information secured by the
Yen Tai News Agency ( ), the Japanese authorities
have long been planning to establish a large shipping
company with the object of monopolizing navigation rights
along the Yangtze River as well as for the purpose of
ousting the shipping trade of Great Britain, the U.S.A.
and other Powers in China.
It is learned that the Nisshin Kisen
Kaisha and other local Japanese shipping companies
have been instructed by the Tokyo Government to dispose
of shares among the public and to instruct the puppet
officials to help in the acceleration of the formation
of this shipping company. All preparations have now
been completed. The new company will be known as the
"Yangtze Shipping Company." The new company was
inaugurated at the Astor House Hotel the other day when
about 50 directors and committeemen were elected and one
Pan was elected comprador.
The company will engage in the
transportation of cargo to various ports along the Yangtsze
as from January next year. It will operate 16 new steamers.
This shows Japan's ambition to control navigation in the
Yangtsze. Not only will ●se navigation rights in Central
China be under the complete control of the Japanese,
but Britain, America and other foreign countries will
have very little hope of recovering their trade along
the Yangtsze for they will not be in a position to compete
with the Japanese.

日本人组建大型航运公司以经营长江贸易

据烟台新闻社 ( ) 获得的消息，日本当局长期以来一直计划成立一家大型航运公司，目的是垄断长江航行权，并排挤英国、美国及其他列强在中国的航运贸易。
据悉，日清汽船株式会社及其他当地日本航运公司已接到东京政府的指示，向公众出售股份，并指示傀儡官员协助加速成立该航运公司。目前所有准备工作均已就绪。新公司将命名为“长江轮船公司”。日前，该公司在外滩礼查饭店 (Astor House Hotel) 举行成立仪式，选举了约50名董事和委员，并选举潘某为买办。
该公司将从明年一月起从事向长江各港口运输货物的业务。它将运营16艘新轮船。这显示了日本控制长江航行的野心。不仅华中地区的航行权将完全处于日本人的控制之下，而且英国、美国和其他外国国家恢复其长江贸易的希望也非常渺茫，因为他们将无法与日本人竞争。

Japanese Shipping Monopoly
Shanghai Shippers Forced to Sell Ships
At New Company's Own Valuation

BEHIND the simple announcement issued by the Japanese on Thursday concerning the formation of an inland shipping service lies the result of an ingenious, well-prepared and thought-out scheme which is now being put into effect with the assistance of the Japanese Government and Army. By means of this scheme, a Japanese company receives not only the monopolistic rights of navigation in the Shanghai hinterland but the company is also given the right practically to force all shippers interested in this particular trade—British, German, Italian, American, Chinese and others—to hand over all their vessels, in part payment for shares, at the company's own estimate of their value.

The Japanese announcement said that the capital of the company has been fixed at Yen 2,000,000. The "North-China Daily News," as a result of an investigation made on Thursday and yesterday, learns that it will be subscribed as follows:—
Yen 600,000 will be taken up by the Japanese Government;
Yen 600,000 will be taken up by the "Ta Tao" and Nanking government bodies;
Yen 400,000 will be taken up by the O.S.K. (Osaka Shosen Kaisha);
and Yen 400,000 will be available for taking up by the various shippers concerned, whose vessels will make the operation of the company possible.
At the moment, the "North-China Daily News" understands, a deadlock has been reached, despite the announcement issued by the Japanese. The shippers have refused to come in on the unfair terms proposed and the company has the sole right to operate in the area concerned. Out of the 140-odd ships which normally engage in the traffic, less than twenty, which were seized some time ago by the Japanese, are in operation.
The reason for the deadlock is not difficult to find. The new monopoly represents the climax to a four month period of extreme difficulty for the shippers, who have been forced to operate at almost a loss due to the high rates they have been charged by the former "holding, company." In order to make any profit at all, they have been forced to charge three or four times the normal cargo rate, which explains, among other things, the high cost of vegetables and other foodstuffs in Shanghai today.

Position in February
But to go back to the beginning. Shortly before the end of February, an announcement was issued by the Japanese Navy, Army and diplomatic authorities stating that henceforth permits would be required of all vessels plying the main inland waterways, and authorization would be granted free of charge, or in the words of the announcement itself, "the permit will be issued gratis upon due examination of the application." Matters were not quite as simple as all that, however, the shippers soon found, for one difficulty after another arose, permits being refused on the grounds of "necessity," as laid down in clause 2 of the announcement, whereby "such use may temporarily be prohibited or restricted by the Japanese Army and Navy."
A Japanese company—said to have received the backing of the O.S.K.—then appeared on the scene and in their difficulty the shippers perforce accepted the somewhat one-sided plan put forward by this company, styled itself the Kianchek (Kiangsu-Chekiang) Steamship Co.

The First Scheme
The company promised to furnish all ships "co-operating with it" with the necessary Japanese pass; in addition, the ships would be given the right to fly the "Japanese flag and two Japanese would travel with each ship as additional protection. In return, the shippers were to pay the company 50 per cent. of what was termed the net revenue—expenses of the trip, fuel and so on, being first deducted; this, however, did not include office and overhead expenses, which the Japanese company refused to recognize. This was somewhat steep, but it was better than not operating the vessels at all, and the shippers accepted.
The company itself had about 20 vessels; the shippers provided an additional 120 ships.
They soon found things were not moving exactly as smoothly as was hoped. In the first place, the Japanese guards soon found it safer to leave the ships at a point on the Soochow Creek just north of Rubicon Road—after that, it was not safe for them to proceed further, owing to guerillas.
The ships soon got around this difficulty, however, and flew the Japanese flag as far as this point and then, when they had got out of sight, flew the British or American flag when passing through "guerilla country." The ships would sometimes be searched, but otherwise left unharmed by the guerillas.
Then came another difficulty, and a major one. The "holding company" could only provide the ships with permits to move about in the areas concerned—but in order to take cargo in and/or out, another Japanese military pass was required—and this was in nine cases out of ten only issuable to Japanese subjects.

Passes for Sale
Japanese subjects were willing to co-operate at a price, which varied from $500 to $1,000 a trip, when they provided the passes; during June the average Chinese newspaper carried from six to ten advertisements a day, inserted by these Japanese pass-procurers quite boldly.
All this was bad enough, the shippers now complain, but the announcement of June 25, which came like a bolt out of the blue, was too much if a mixed metaphor may be used, it was the last straw which broke the camel's back and heart.
This announcement stated that a new company—styled the China-Japan Inland Navigation Co., or the Shanghai Inland Navigation Co., as they seem to be the same organization—would have the monopoly of business along the various shipping routes in the hinterland. No competition would be permitted.
Shippers of any nationality were given the option of taking up shares in the new company, or of going out of business. At first sight, one might imagine that their choice would be obviously in favour of the former proposition—but there were several major snags.
The "North-China Daily News" has secured one copy of each of the three forms which were sent around to the various companies by the Japanese combine. One sheet calls for particulars of the companies' vessels—age, length, tonnage, haulage power and so on—and the other is an application for an allotment of shares.

Cause of the Trouble
The third (to which the first is to be attached) is the one that has caused most of the trouble. It can best be divided into three sections, which for convenience may be labeled Sections A, B and C.
Section A, to be filled in by the shipper, in which he sets out the estimated value of the craft concerned and also when it was so valued.
Section B, to be filled in by the company's officials later, gives the value of the vessel according to the company's own assessors, and bears the signature of the chairman of the valuation committee.
Section C, to be filled in by the shipper when forwarding the document (and hence before Section B is filled in and before he knows what the company's valuation will be), in which the shipper states that he accepts the company's valuation of it as final; he then signs it.
The application for allotment of shares states that the shares are valued at 50 yen each. A first payment of Yen 12.50 a share is required to be forwarded with the application. The form states that the balance was to be paid in full "before July 20," or the deposit would be forwarded; it is understood, however, that in view of the lack of what might be termed "popular response" among shippers, the date has been set back slightly. Collection would be made at the Yokohama Specie Bank offices at either Shanghai or Tokyo.

At a Deadlock
At the moment, therefore, matters are at a deadlock. Shippers cannot operate under the old scheme, and they cannot see their way towards "co-operating" with the new plan. In the first place, most of them do not wish to lose most of their rights, as they would when they became the minority in the new large company, nor are they willing to accept the company's valuation of their vessels "as final".
In interviews with the "North-China Daily News," shippers pointed out that, technically speaking, the Japanese company could value a $5,000-craft as worth $5—and the unfortunate shipper would not be able to do anything about it. It is understood that one German concern and a few Chinese firms have wavered and thrown in their lot with the Japanese—deeming it the better part of a bad bargain—but the others are still obdurate.
The position at the moment, therefore, is that the company cannot operate without the boats, and the shippers cannot operate without the permits held by the company.

日本航运垄断
上海船主被迫按新公司自行估价出售船只

在日本周四发布的关于成立内河航运服务的简单公告背后，隐藏着一个巧妙、精心准备且经过深思熟虑的计划的成果，该计划目前正借助日本政府和军队的协助付诸实施。通过这一计划，一家日本公司不仅获得了在上海腹地航行的垄断权，而且该公司还实际上有权迫使所有从事此项特定贸易的船主——包括英国、德国、意大利、美国、中国及其他国家的船主——按照该公司自行估算的价值，将其所有船只移交，作为部分股款以换取股份。

日本方面的公告称，该公司的资本额定为200万日元。《字林西报》经周四和昨日的调查获悉，股本认购情况如下：
日本政府认购60万日元；
“大陶”（Ta Tao）及南京政府机构认购60万日元；
大阪商船会社（O.S.K.）认购40万日元；
另有40万日元可供相关各船主认购，正是这些船主的船只使公司的运营成为可能。
据《字林西报》目前了解，尽管日本方面发布了公告，但局势已陷入僵局。船主们拒绝接受所提出的不公平条款，而该公司拥有在该地区运营的唯一权利。在通常从事此项运输的大约140艘船只中，只有不到20艘仍在运营，这些船只是一些时候前被日本人扣押的。

造成僵局的原因不难寻找。这一新的垄断局面标志着船主们为期四个月的极度困难时期达到了顶峰，由于前任“控股公司”收取的高额费用，他们几乎是在亏本运营。为了获得任何利润，他们被迫收取正常运费三到四倍的货物运费，这也解释了除其他因素外，上海今日蔬菜和其他食品价格高昂的原因。

二月的局势
但让我们回到起点。二月下旬前不久，日本海军、陆军及外交当局发布了一则公告，声明此后所有行驶于主要内河水道的船只均需许可证，并将免费授予授权，或者用公告自己的话说，“经适当审查申请后，将免费发放许可证”。然而，事情并不像看起来那么简单，船主们很快发现，困难接踵而至，许可证以公告第二条规定的“必要性”为由被拒绝，该条规定“日本陆海军可暂时禁止或限制此类使用”。

随后，一家据称得到大阪商船会社（O.S.K.）支持的日本公司出现在舞台上，处于困境中的船主们被迫接受了这家公司提出的略显片面的计划，该公司自称为“江浙轮船公司”（Kianchek Steamship Co.）。

第一个方案
该公司承诺向所有“与其合作”的船只提供必要的日本通行证；此外，这些船只将被允许悬挂“日本国旗”，并有两名日本人随每艘船同行以提供额外保护。作为回报，船主需向该公司支付所谓净收入的50%——即先扣除航程费用、燃料费等；但这并不包括办公和管理费用，日本公司拒绝承认这些费用。这条件相当苛刻，但总比完全无法运营船只要好，因此船主们接受了。
该公司自身拥有约20艘船只；船主们提供了额外的120艘船只。

他们很快发现事情进展并不如预期的那样顺利。首先，日本护卫人员很快发现，将船只留在苏州河鲁必登路（Rubicon Road）以北的一个地点更为安全——在此之后，由于游击队的存在，继续前行对他们来说并不安全。
船只很快克服了这一困难，悬挂日本国旗航行至该点，然后，当驶离视线进入“游击区”时，便改挂英国或美国国旗。船只有时会受到搜查，但 otherwise 未受游击队伤害。

接着出现了另一个困难，而且是一个主要的困难。“控股公司”只能为船只提供在相关区域移动的许可证——但为了进出货物，还需要另一份日本军事通行证——而在十有八九的情况下，这种通行证只发给日本臣民。

通行证买卖
日本臣民愿意在有偿条件下合作，当他们提供通行证时，每次航程的价格从500美元到1,000美元不等；六月期间，平均每家中文报纸每天刊登六到十则由这些日本通行证代办人 boldly 插入的广告。

船主们现在抱怨说，这一切已经够糟糕了，但6月25日的公告犹如晴天霹雳，如果可以使用混合隐喻的话，这真是压垮骆驼背脊和心灵的最后一根稻草。
该公告声明，一家新公司——名为中日内河航运公司，或上海内河航运公司，因为它们似乎是同一组织——将垄断腹地各航运路线的业务。不允许任何竞争。
任何国籍的船主都被给予选择：要么认购新公司的股份，要么停业。乍一看，人们可能会认为他们的选择显然倾向于前者——但存在几个主要障碍。
《字林西报》已获得日本财团发送给各公司的三种表格的各一份副本。一张表格要求填写公司船只的详细信息——船龄、长度、吨位、牵引力等——另一张则是股份配发申请书。

麻烦的起因
第三张表格（第一张需附在其上）是造成大部分麻烦的原因。它可以最好地分为三个部分，为方便起见，可标记为A、B和C部分。
A部分，由船主填写，在其中列明相关船只的估计价值以及估值时间。
B部分，稍后由公司官员填写，根据该公司自有评估师确定船只价值，并附有估值委员会主席的签名。
C部分，由船主在递交文件时填写（因此在B部分填写之前，且在他知道公司估值是多少之前），在其中船主声明他接受公司对该船只的估值为最终结果；然后他签字。
股份配发申请书指出，每股价值50日元。申请时需随附每股12.50日元的首付款。表格规定余款需在“7月20日之前”全额付清，否则定金将被没收；但据悉，鉴于船主中缺乏所谓的“积极响应”，截止日期已略微推迟。收款将在横滨正金银行上海或东京办事处进行。

陷入僵局
因此，目前局势陷入僵局。船主们无法在旧方案下运营，也看不出如何与新计划“合作”。首先，他们大多数人不愿失去大部分权利，因为一旦成为新大型公司中的少数派，他们就会失去这些权利；他们也不愿接受公司对其船只的估值为“最终结果”。
在接受《字林西报》采访时，船主们指出，从技术上讲，日本公司可以将一艘价值5,000美元的船只估价为5美元——而不幸的船主对此将无能为力。据悉，一家德国企业和几家中国公司曾犹豫不决，最终选择与日本人合作——认为这是在糟糕交易中较好的选择——但其他公司仍然固执己见。
因此，目前的局势是：没有船只，公司无法运营；而没有公司持有的许可证，船主们也无法运营。

Office are secretly agitating for the abolition of the Japanese

by the "Kiangsu-Chekiang Steamship Navigation Company" which

the Nisshin Kisen Kaisha, 5 The Bund, the Yamashita Kisen

据报，日本总领事馆正在对所有在上海与内地之间运营小轮（launches）的轮船公司进行注册，外资拥有的公司除外。无需缴纳注册费或押金，注册将基于公司的财务状况和经营业务，并依据知名日本商号的推荐信予以批准。日本总领事馆进行注册，可能是由于某些轮船公司提出的交涉所致。4月底，日本军方曾试图对所有轮船公司进行注册，并指令每家公司缴纳500美元注册费和10,000美元现金押金，但据报道只有少数公司遵守了这一命令。然而，那些已注册的公司所缴纳的押金，在日本总领事馆于4月24日取代日本军方开始进行注册时已被退还，但对于500美元的注册费则只字未提。

Japanese Control Rice
Supplies
Merchants Asked to Register
With Military
The purchase of Chinese rice in
Japanese-occupied areas outside
Shanghai is virtually under the con-
trol of the Japanese military authori-
ties, according to a Chinese report.
Rice merchants wishing to buy rice
from these districts will have to
register with the Japanese and pay
a registration fee of $500 in addition
to a cash security of $10,000. Rice
purchased by non-registered mer-
chants is liable to confiscation by the
Japanese, the same report says.
Merchants desirous to register with
the Japanese often experience all
kinds of difficulties. Registered mer-
chants also find it difficult to transport
rice to Shanghai as they have to pass
through many barriers on the way.
Rice produced at Wusih costs $6.50
a picul and that at Tsingpu, $7 a picul.
As the merchants are required to
pay taxes to the so-called autono-
mous commissions on the way to
Shanghai, the cost of Wusih or Tsing-
pu products becomes about $10 per
picul.
The daily consumption in Shanghai
has increased from 6,000 piculs of
rice to 10,000 piculs, according to the
report. The stocks in Shanghai con-
sist of 150,000 piculs Chinese rice
and 50,000 piculs foreign rice at
present. It is reported that large
quantities of foreign rice are being
imported.
page_data.zh:
日本控制大米
供应
商人被要求向军方
注册
据一份中文报告称，在上海以外的日军占领区购买中国大米实际上处于日本军方的控制之下。希望从这些地区购买大米的米商必须向日本方面注册，并支付500美元的注册费，此外还需缴纳10,000美元的现金保证金。该报告还称，非注册商人购买的大米可能会被日本方面没收。
希望向日本方面注册的商人常常遇到各种困难。已注册的商人也将大米运往上海时发现困难重重，因为他们途中必须通过许多关卡。
无锡产的大米价格为每担6.50美元，青浦产的大米为每担7美元。由于商人在运往上海的途中被要求向所谓的“自治委员会”缴纳税款，无锡或青浦产品的成本变为每担约10美元。
据该报告称，上海的日消费量已从6,000担大米增加到10,000担。目前上海的库存包括150,000担中国大米和50,000担外国大米。据报道，大量外国大米正在进口中。

page_data.en:
No Reason For
Alarm Seen In
Rice Situation

Despite reports that Chinese rice
in Japanese-occupied areas is under
the control of Japanese military
authorities, who exact heavy fees
from purchasers, local circles are
not inclined to feel that the city's
supply of the grain is seriously
threatened.
It is pointed out that during the
early days of the hostilities the
situation was considerably worse,
and that Chinese rice was not
available at any price—except for
the small quantity in local store-
rooms.
The city, at that time consuming
approximately 10,000 piculs daily,
depended entirely upon imported
rice, largely from Indo-China,
whose sale was controlled by the
Shanghai Municipal Council in
order to eliminate possible racke-
teering and profiteering at the ex-
pense of the populace.
It is stated that if the situation
becomes intolerable, and if the fees
demanded of dealers purchasing
rice in Japanese-occupied areas
are such as to make the native
product more expensive than im-
ported rice, arrangements will again
be made to import the grain from
Indo-China.
According to local reports, rice
merchants who purchase the native
grain from areas under Nipponese
occupancy are required to pay a
registration fee of $500 in addition
to a cash security of $10,000.
Otherwise, rice purchased by non-
registered dealers is liable to con-
fiscation, reports state.

page_data.zh:
大米局势中
未见恐慌
理由

尽管有报道称日军占领区的中国大米处于日本军方的控制之下，且向购买者收取高额费用，但本地各界并不认为该市的大米供应受到严重威胁。
有人指出，在战事初期，情况要糟糕得多，当时除了本地仓库中的少量存货外，无论出什么价格都买不到中国大米。
当时该市每天消耗约10,000担大米，完全依赖进口大米，主要来自印度支那，其销售由上海公共租界工部局控制，以消除可能出现的敲诈勒索和牺牲民众利益的牟取暴利行为。
据称，如果局势变得无法忍受，且向在日军占领区购买大米的经销商收取的费用使得国产大米比进口大米更昂贵，则将再次安排从印度支那进口粮食。
据本地报道，从日占区购买国产大米的米商被要求支付500美元的注册费，此外还需缴纳10,000美元的现金保证金。否则，据报道，非注册经销商购买的大米可能会被没收。

Permits For
Ships Plying
China Waters

Japanese Authorities
Issue New Set Of
Regulations

NO CHARGE WILL BE
MADE FOR PERMITS

Pleasure Craft Are Asked
Also To Make Regular
Application

Permits will be required of
all vessels plying main inland
waterways in the Central
China areas now under Japan-
ese control, the Japanese Navy,
Army and diplomatic authori-
ties in Shanghai announced
last night.

The permits, issued by the Japan-
ese naval and military authorities,
will be necessitated for pleasure as
well as business craft. The author-
ization will be granted free of
charge, the announcement stated.
Any ship contravening this rule
will be subject to seizure, together
with its cargo.

Text Of The Rules
The announcement, in full, was
as follows:
“I.—For the time being, naviga-
tion by all steamships and motor
boats, other than those possessing
‘inland stream navigation permits’
issued by the Japanese Army and
Navy authorities, is hereby prohibit-
ed on the following water routes
located in areas now under the con-
trol of the Japanese Army and
Navy:
“(a) Shanghai—Sungkiang (Pung-
llamao)—Pinghu.
“(b) Shanghai—Sungkiang — Kashing
—Hangchow
“(c) Shanghai — Sungkiang — Ping-
wang—Wushing.
“(d) Shanghai—Hwangtu—Chukiakio.
“(e) Shanghai—Quinsan—Soochow.
—Wusin — Wutsin—Tanyang —
Chikiang.
“(f) Shanghai—Quinsan—Changshin—
Soochow.
“(g) Shanghai — Kating — Taitang—
Changshin.
“(h) Shanghai—Tsungming Island—
Tungchow.
“Boats propelled by man-power,
while exempted from this rule,
must obtain the above-mentioned
permit.
“Any ship contravening this rule
shall be subject to seizure, together
with its cargo.

Mode Of Application
“A person desiring to obtain the
above-mentioned permit must submit
two copies—one each to the Chiefs
of the Special Service Departments
of the Army and Navy respectively
—of an application clearly setting
forth therein the name of the ship,
the names of the owner and the
persons employed on the ship, and
the route, period and purpose for
which the permit is sought. The
permit will be issued gratis upon
due examination of the application.
“2.—No special restriction is im-
posed upon the use of small streams
or local routes not included in the
above list. In case of necessity,
however, such use may temporarily
be prohibited or restricted by the
Japanese Army and Navy.
“3.—Use of the routes mentioned
in the preceding paragraph will be
permitted only as far as the nearest
locality in which an office of the
Kiangche Steamship Company is
situated.
“4.—No special restriction is im-
posed upon navigation by ships for
purposes other than that of busi-
ness. But even in the case of such
ships, permits will be required for
passage through the routes included
in the above list.”

在中国水域
航行船只的
许可证

日本当局
颁布新一套
规章

许可证不
收取费用

游乐船只也被要求
按规定申请

昨晚，驻上海的日本海军、陆军及外交当局宣布，目前在日军控制下的华中地区，所有在主要内河航道航行的船只均需办理许可证。

该许可证由日本海陆军事当局签发，无论是游乐船只还是商业船只均需办理。公告称，此项授权将免费授予。任何违反此规定的船只及其货物将被扣押。

规章全文
公告全文如下：
“一、即日起，禁止所有不具备日本陆海军当局签发的‘内河航行许可证’的轮船和摩托艇在下列位于日本陆海军控制区域内的水道航行：
“(a) 上海—松江（Pungllamao）—平湖。
“(b) 上海—松江—嘉兴—杭州
“(c) 上海—松江—平望—吴兴。
“(d) 上海—黄渡—朱家角。
“(e) 上海—昆山—苏州。
—吴江—乌镇—丹阳—
镇江。
“(f) 上海—昆山—常熟—
苏州。
“(g) 上海—嘉定—太仓—
常熟。
“(h) 上海—崇明岛—
通州。
“人力驱动的船只虽免于此规定，但仍须获得上述许可证。
“任何违反此规定的船只及其货物将被扣押。

申请方式
“欲获得上述许可证的人必须提交两份申请书——分别提交给陆军和海军特务机关长——申请书中需清楚列明船只名称、船主及船上受雇人员的姓名，以及申请许可证的航线、期限和目的。经适当审查申请书后，将免费颁发许可证。
“二、对于未列入上述名单的小河流或地方航线的使用，不设特别限制。但在必要时，日本陆海军可暂时禁止或限制此类使用。
“三、前段所述航线的使用，仅允许至设有江浙轮船公司办事处的最近地点为止。

Made by C.D.I. Sih Tsu-liang Forwarded by C Crawford

Forward herewith is a list of thirty-five steamship
companies and one public ferry which are at present main-
taining communications between Shanghai and inland places.
Thirty-one of these steamship companies are located
in the International Settlement while the remainder are in
the French Concession.
Of these companies, twelve are Chinese owned, while
twenty-four ostensibly belong to foreign interests; namely
British (6), German (4) Italian (4), Japanese (5), Portuguese
(3), American (1) and Netherlands (1).
Information has now been received to the effect that
the passes issued to steam launch owners by the Japanese
Military authorities and the Dah Dao City Government permitting
them to operate in the area now under the control of the
Japanese Military will become invalid on March 15.
A new organ entitled the "Kiangsu Chekiang Steamboat
Company (江浙輪船公司)" has recently been established at
793, Soochow Road, by the Nisshin Kaisen Kaisha, for the
purpose of dealing with applications of steamboat owners for
new passes. Fees charged for new passes are not fixed but
are to be decided upon in different cases.

Subject Kiangsu-Chekiang Steamship Navigation Company - Establishment of.
Made by and Forwarded by Inspector Papp.

According to information received, the Japanese
Authorities are now planning to exercise control over local
shipping. Since the evacuation of Chinese troops from
Shanghai, various foreign and Chinese shipping concerns which
operated lines between Shanghai and various interior cities
have secured passes and permits from Japanese military and
naval authorities through foreign consuls. Owing to the
urgent need of communication facilities after the war, these
shipping companies as a rule made a considerable amount of
money in a short space of time.
It has now been learned that in compliance with
repeated requests of their business men, the Japanese Authorities
have decided to cancel all such passes and permits issued,
effective from March 10, and have given permission to the
organization of a new shipping concern which has been named
"The Kiangsu-Chekiang Steamship Navigation Company". The
new concern has recently been organized under the joint auspices
of three Japanese shipping companies here, namely, the Nisshin
Kisen Kaisha, 5 The Bund, the Yamashita Kisen Kaisha, 30 Foochow
Road, and the Showa Shipping Co. Ltd., 130 Hankow Road. The
new concern is planning to operate a fleet of about 100 steamers
and steam launches in the interior of Kiangsu and Chekiang
provinces. Six shipping lines have been mapped out and will
be operated exclusively by the Company as follows:-
(1) Shanghai to Hangchow, (2) Shanghai to Wusih, (3) Shanghai
to Changshu(常熟), (4) Shanghai to Pinghu (平湖), (5) Shanghai

由帕普（Papp）巡官撰写并呈报。

据所获情报，日本当局目前正计划对本地航运业实施控制。自中国军队撤离上海以来，经营上海与各内地城市之间航线的各家外国及中国航运公司，已通过外国领事馆从日本海陆军当局处获得了通行证和许可证。由于战后对交通设施的迫切需求，这些航运公司通常在短时间内赚取了巨额利润。

现获悉，应其商界人士的反复请求，日本当局已决定自3月10日起取消所有已签发的此类通行证和许可证，并批准组建一家名为“江苏浙江轮船公司”的新航运企业。这家新企业最近在上海三家日本航运公司的共同支持下组建而成，这三家公司分别是：位于外滩5号的日清汽船株式会社（Nisshin Kisen Kaisha）、位于福州路30号的山下汽船株式会社（Yamashita Kisen Kaisha），以及位于汉口路130号的昭和海运株式会社（Showa Shipping Co. SHIPPING REVIVED
INTO INTERIOR
Many New Companies
Operating Out Of
Shanghai Now

With new shipping firms run by
foreign interests springing up al-
most daily in Shanghai, navigation
between this city and other im-
portant cities in the interior of
Kiangsu and Chekiang is no more
the problem it proved soon after
the conclusion of hostilities in and
around Shanghai, investigations re-
vealed yesterday.

A new Japanese firm, the Shang-
hai Shipping Company, has just
been established here. It was
officially announced by this com-
pany yesterday that a steamer
would go to Quinsan, Paichen,
Soochow and Wusih early to-
morrow morning, stopping at all
points of call. Several junks will
be towed by the steamer so that
goods may be transported to the
interior where cigarettes and other
sundry goods are urgently needed.

Competing with this new Japan-
ese firm is a number of other for-
eign shipping firms established by
British, American, German and
Portuguese merchants, which are
maintaining boats on regular runs
between important districts of
Tsinpu, Quinsan, Soochow, Wusih,
Changshu, Huchow and Pinghu.

Rice merchants in Shanghai are
greatly benefited by these shipping
firms, for it is no longer a problem
to transport Chinese rice to Shang-
hai from rice-producing districts
in Kiangsu and Chekiang, notably
Changshu. These companies are
trying to find more ships.

A steamer belonging to another
Japanese shipping firm left Shang-
hai yesterday morning for Pinghu,
carrying cargo and about 40 pass-
engers. The boat will have to pass
Minghong, Sungkiang, Chukiang
and another district before reach-
ing its destination. The steamer
left the Canton Road Bund yester-
day at about 9 a.m. after some
hours delay. It was the first run
of the vessel.

运营

随着由外国利益集团经营的新航运公司在上海几乎每日涌现，调查显示，昨日上海与江苏、浙江内地其他重要城市之间的航行，已不再是上海及周边战事结束后不久曾显现出的那样一个问题。

一家新的日本公司，上海航运公司（Shanghai Shipping Company），刚刚在此成立。该公司昨日正式宣布，一艘轮船将于明早启程前往昆山、白茆（音译）、苏州和无锡，并在所有停靠点停留。几艘驳船将由该轮船拖带，以便将货物运往急需香烟和其他杂项货物的内地。

与这家新的日本公司竞争的还有其他一些由英国、美国、德国和葡萄牙商人建立的外国航运公司，它们在青浦、昆山、苏州、无锡、常熟、湖州和平湖等重要地区之间维持着定期航班。

上海的米商极大地受益于这些航运公司，因为将中国大米从江苏和浙江的产米区（尤其是常熟）运往上海已不再是个问题。这些公司正试图寻找更多的船只。

另一家日本航运公司的一艘轮船于昨晨离开上海前往平湖，载有货物和约40名乘客。该船在抵达目的地前必须经过闵行、松江、朱泾（音译）和其他地区。该轮船在延误数小时后，于昨日上午9点左右离开广东路外滩。这是该船的首航。
